newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank rate cut call seen appropriate.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank rate cut call seen appropriate.

text.p: Financial analysts said the Bank of Thailand's call on banks to cut interest rates on Tuesday was an appropriate move because inflation was in check and the sluggish economy needed a boost.

But any quick and sharp reductions in rates by banks were unlikely because of a lack of clarity on the level of liquidity in the local system and political uncertainty after Sunday's election, they said.
Thailand has some of the highest rates in the region with the Minimum Lending Rate ranging from 13.25 to 13.50 percent.
The winner of the Thai election, the New Aspiration Party's Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, has formed a six-party coalition that is set to become the next government with him as prime minister.
Analysts were anxious to see how his economic ministers would handle the rates issue.

"The central bank may have some degree of confidence that the inflation is not worrisome and be in check," said Teera Ashakul, the head of research department at Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT). "When inflation falls, a cut in interest rates is practical," he added.
Thailand's consumer price index in October rose 4.3 percent year-on-year, the slowest growth rate in three years, against 4.6 percent in the same month a year ago.
The year-on-year monthly inflation rate rose as high as 7.4 percent early this year.
Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond has said commercial banks should cut their lending and deposit interest rates to help boost the slowing economy.
A reduction in local interest rates would also help boost sluggish credit growth which rose only 16 to 17 percent this year, he added.
"I am confident that a cut in local deposit and lending interest rates will not undermine the economic stability," he said.
The Thai economy has slowed significantly with private analysts' predicting gross domestic product growth of above 6.0 percent in 1996 from 8.6 percent in 1995.
The economy expanded at about nine percent annually for a decade before last year.
This year, exports growth has also been sluggish and private investment remained slow, analysts said.

"Everyone acknowledges that the economy is slowing and many major industries like property sector are being affected," central bank governor Rerngchai said. "Therefore local interest rates should be lowered to help bolster the economy."
Bankers said they welcomed Rerngchai's remarks.

"The remarks gave a positive signal for banks to cut their interest rates. But political concern and volatility in market liquidity will prevent sharp falls in interest rates," said one senior treasurer at a European bank.
The IFCT's Teera said: "The cut in interest rates will prevent the economy from hard landing. Our economy has been adversely affected by the central bank's tight monetary policy early this year."
